question: What are Alphabet, Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft each currently guiding for capital expenditures, and how do they line up on a calendar-2026 basis?
grading: Reference-free recency: use each company’s latest guide before the run timestamp, date it and preserve its calendar/fiscal and lease definitions. At the October 1 snapshot, CY2026: Alphabet $195–205B; Meta $130–145B including finance-lease principal; Amazon ~$220B cash capex; Microsoft ~$175B including finance leases/excluding operating leases. Do not treat Microsoft’s fiscal FY2027 or Q1 figures as calendar totals, or invent a harmonized cash basis.
answer: As of October 1, 2026, all four provide calendar-2026 capex numbers: Alphabet USD 195–205 billion (July 22 Q2 call); [G28-E1] Meta USD 130–145 billion including finance-lease principal payments (July 29 Q2 release); [G28-E2] Amazon approximately USD 220 billion in cash capex (July 30 Q2 call); [G28-E3] Microsoft approximately USD 175 billion (July 29 FY2026 Q4 call), including finance leases but excluding operating leases. Microsoft lowered the displayed capex amount because extending building useful lives shifts some future leases to operating classification; investment expectations apart from that change were unchanged. [G28-E4] Nominal ordering is Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, but the lease definitions differ, so these are not fully harmonized cash-spending measures. Microsoft separately expects FY2027 capex to grow YoY and Q1 FY2027 capex above USD 50 billion; those fiscal guides are not additional CY2026 totals. [G28-E4]

output.answer:
Here are the **calendar-2026 capex guidance** figures for the four hyperscalers, ranked from highest to lowest:

| Company | Calendar 2026 Capex Guidance |
|---------|------------------------------|
| **Amazon** | ~**$220 billion** (raised from prior $200B guide) |
| **Alphabet** | **$195–$205 billion** |
| **Microsoft** | ~**$175 billion** |
| **Meta** | **$130–$145 billion** |

**How they line up:**  
- **Amazon** is the biggest spender at ~$220B, driven by AWS infrastructure demand (Q2 AWS revenue grew 37% to $42.2B with a $496B backlog).
- **Alphabet** comes in second at $195–$205B; Sundar Pichai raised the 2026 outlook, sending the stock down 7% on the news.
- **Microsoft** is guiding roughly $175B for calendar 2026 (note: its fiscal year ends June 30, but this is the calendar-year figure cited by management).
- **Meta** is the smallest of the four at $130–$145B, though that still represents nearly doubling its 2025 full-year spend.

**Combined:** These four are expected to spend roughly **$720–$745 billion** on capex in 2026 (one estimate pegs the total around $760B), with most of the investment going into AI infrastructure and data-center buildouts.

Sources:  
- Forbes: Microsoft ~$175B calendar 2026 capex ([forbes.com](https://www.forbes.com/sites/greatspeculations/2026/10/01/what-could-move-microsoft-in-the-next-six-months))  
- Yahoo Finance: Amazon ~$220B, Alphabet $195–$205B ([yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/amazon-raised-2026-capex-guide-114017457.html), [yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/ai-capex-creates-investment-cycle-152100533.html))  
- Yahoo Finance: Meta $130–$145B ([yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/meta-become-mega-cloud-operator-154422140.html), [yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/meta-now-owes-22-billion-112355817.html))  
- Yahoo Finance: Combined ~$760B total for the four ([yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/760-billion-ai-risk-nobody-112300734.html))
